_about: Question-specific grading criteria and follow-ups, keyed by question id. Overrides the generic defaults from the export script. Each criterion is one checkable thing a strong answer contains. See .agents/skills/interview-question/SKILL.md.

criteria: Names the 28-point train/validation gap as high variance (overfitting)
Proposes constraining the tree: max_depth, min_samples_leaf or pruning
Mentions averaging trees (random forest) as an alternative
Says what to check if the gap persists: leakage, label noise or a shifted validation set
classical-ml-questions:cml-high-variance.followup: You limit depth and validation stays at 71%. What do you look at next?

criteria: Identifies low, close train and validation scores as high bias (underfitting)
Uses the 95% human score as the reference for how much is achievable
Proposes more capacity, better features, less regularisation or longer training
Explains why collecting more data will not fix underfitting
classical-ml-questions:cml-high-bias.followup: How would you know you had fixed bias and not just moved to overfitting?

criteria: Computes 10,000 × 4/5 = 8,000 training rows per model
Notes each row is used for validation exactly once across the five runs
classical-ml-questions:cml-kfold-rows.followup: When is k-fold cross-validation the wrong choice?

criteria: Explains that random folds put future days in training (temporal leakage)
Proposes a time-based split: train before a cut-off, test after
Mentions a rolling or expanding window for repeated evaluation
States the principle: validation must mimic how the model is used in production
classical-ml-questions:cml-time-series-s.followup: How large a gap would you leave between the training cut-off and the test window, and why?

criteria: Asks whether the value is known at prediction time
Recognises account_closure_reason is written when the outcome happens (target leakage)
Removes the feature and anything derived from it
Expects AUC to drop to a believable number and treats 0.99 as a warning sign
classical-ml-questions:cml-leaky-feature.followup: How would you catch this kind of leak automatically before training?

criteria: Explains SMOTE interpolates between real minority points
Identifies that resampling before the split leaks near-copies of test rows into training
Fixes it: split first, resample only the training data, inside a pipeline per CV fold
Questions whether resampling is needed at all versus class weights and threshold tuning
classical-ml-questions:cml-smote-before-.followup: Do you need resampling at all here?

criteria: Computes precision = 15 / 50 = 0.3
Interprets it: 30% of flagged transactions are fraud
Names who bears the cost of low precision (the review team)
classical-ml-questions:cml-precision.followup: Who in the business cares most about precision here, and why?

criteria: Computes recall = 15 / 20 = 0.75
Interprets it: the model catches three quarters of the fraud
Explains that lowering the threshold raises recall and usually lowers precision
classical-ml-questions:cml-recall.followup: How would you raise recall, and what does it cost?

criteria: Explains the harmonic mean is pulled towards the lower of precision and recall
Names a case where F1 is the wrong metric (unequal error costs)
classical-ml-questions:cml-f1.followup: When would you not use F1 to choose between two models?

criteria: Explains 99% accuracy is what always predicting 'not fraud' scores
Recommends precision and recall at the operating threshold
Recommends PR-AUC for comparing models on the rare class
Explains why ROC-AUC can look optimistic under heavy imbalance
classical-ml-questions:cml-accuracy-imba.followup: Why can ROC-AUC look good while the model is useless for the rare class?

criteria: Works through a concrete population (e.g. 100,000 people: 100 sick, 99 true positives, 999 false positives)
Computes the positive predictive value ≈ 99 / 1,098 ≈ 0.09
Explains that a rare condition makes even an accurate test mostly produce false positives
Connects it to Bayes' rule or the base rate
classical-ml-questions:cml-base-rate.followup: How would you change the screening process to make a positive result more trustworthy?

criteria: Lets the review capacity (200 cases a day) set the threshold: rank and take the top k
Evaluates with precision@k
Compares the cost of missed fraud with the cost of a review
Mentions revisiting the threshold as fraud volume or model scores drift
classical-ml-questions:cml-threshold-cap.followup: Fraud volume doubles next month. What changes in your threshold policy?

criteria: Distinguishes ranking quality (AUC) from probability accuracy (calibration)
Checks a reliability diagram or Brier score
Fixes miscalibration with Platt scaling or isotonic regression on held-out data
Explains why prices need calibrated probabilities, not just a good ranking
classical-ml-questions:cml-calibration.followup: Which would you pick, Platt scaling or isotonic regression, with 2,000 validation examples?

criteria: Computes −ln(0.9) ≈ 0.105
Contrasts it with a confident miss: −ln(0.1) ≈ 2.30
Explains log loss punishes confident wrong predictions heavily
classical-ml-questions:cml-log-loss.followup: Why might a team choose log loss over accuracy when training and comparing models?
